The data has 10868 rows and 6 columns, each row representing death counts by cause, year, and state (or US total).

All causes accounted for a total of about 168 million deaths over the years, with 'All causes' itself representing 56.8% of deaths, showing it may overlap or represent aggregated totals.

- Heart disease caused 14.5% of deaths, the largest single cause excluding the aggregate.
- Cancer caused 12.9%, also a major cause.
- Stroke, CLRD (Chronic Lower Respiratory Disease), and unintentional injuries contributed 3.2%, 3.1%, and 2.8%, respectively.
- Suicides were the smallest category here, at 0.8% of deaths.
- Total deaths show a rising trend from 8.59 million in 1999 up to 9.79 million in 2017.

The trends over years indicate an overall increase in yearly deaths. The main causes make up the majority of the total deaths beyond just the aggregate all-cause column.

The best visualizations are a line chart showing the total deaths trend over years, and a horizontal bar chart showing the death shares by cause sorted descending.

I have saved these two charts as images.
